1821fd3c-40e5-488b-afd7-a03c5454d198: One project I would pick is my real-time vision work for an autonomous badminton-training robot at InnoX. I built the perception pipeline that combined YOLOv8 player detection, pose estimation, shuttlecock tracking, court localization, stereo 3D tracking, and landing-point prediction, reaching 20+ FPS. My main ownership was the system path from camera input to robot-usable perception outputs, including the inference optimization choices on Raspberry Pi. The tradeoff I wrestled with was speed versus model and pipeline fidelity: ONNX Runtime, quantization, and asynchronous video processing made real-time inference feasible, but they also forced me to be careful about timing alignment and not treating model accuracy in isolation from serving constraints. I learned that deploying ML is often an infrastructure problem as much as a modeling problem: latency, throughput, hardware limits, and clean interfaces determine whether a model is actually usable in a real system.
